leftEvidence.title: Christ dies for weak, ungodly, sinful, hostile people and reconciliation follows

points.label: People before change
points.left: Weak, ungodly, sinners, and enemies describe the people in Romans.
points.right: Those for whom one died and the world being reconciled describe the scope in Corinthians.

points.label: Changes named
points.left: Justification by blood, rescue, reconciliation, and rejoicing are named.
points.right: Living for the one who died, changed regard, new creation, reconciliation, and entrusted speech are named.

payload.posture: The sources independently preserve the relationship named by enemies reconciled / one died for all.

rightEvidence.title: One dies for all, changed life follows, and the reconciling message is entrusted

payload.tension: Both passages connect death and reconciliation while arranging the actors, scope, and consequences differently.
payload.title: Enemies reconciled / one died for all
